newsitem.title: USA: Goldman sees slower Japan US debt purchases - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Goldman sees slower Japan US debt purchases - WSJ.

text.p: Certain traders are saying there is cause to question whether Japanese institutions, known for buying U.S. Treasury debt securities over the past year-and-a-half, will continue doing so, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
Foreign governments, including Japan, have bought three-quarters or more of all new securities issued by the U.S. government over the past year, the story says.
The story quotes Goldman Sachs International Vice Chairman Robert Hormats as saying Japanese institutions will likely slow their purchases, which could begin to push up interest rates.
"It could be the Achilles' heel of the bond and stock markets," Hormats tells the newspaper.
